text:
Anika Patel: heads-up — ACME asked for a longer deprecation runway for pinned models. they specifically requested a soft-retire option + clear rollback path. want to draft a playbook?
Liam Cho: ack. are they on dedicated or hosted?
Anika Patel: hosted, high usage, some routes pinned to older quantized variants. they say migration caused perf regressions in evaluation.
Maya Rivera: quick note — our current standard is 30d notice + 7d rollback window. have we published exceptions? :thinking_face:
Carlos (CS): ACME is big customer, they want 90d and migration credits. also asked for canary lanes and a way to opt back to old model temporarily if latency spikes.
Nora Eng: technically we can support opt-back by keeping a compatible pinned artifact and routing by tag for N days. cost + infra considerations though.
Anika Patel: proposed playbook draft in bullets, want feedback:
- announce: 60d public notice to customers (extendable on case-by-case)
- soft-retire window: 60d where pinned version still accepted but rate-limited for new sessions
- migration canary: 14d canary cohort (10% traffic) with automated quality/regression checks
- rollback window: maintain old model artifact + routing for 30d after retirement complete for emergency opt-back
- incentives: migration credits + dedicated SRE support for first 14d
Liam Cho: that seems reasonable. question: how do we define "regression" during canary? absolute drop in eval f1? or SLO impact?
Maya Rivera: recommend hybrid — require both: (a) customer-specific eval suite pass rate >= baseline - 2% AND (b) latency p95 within 1.2x baseline. both checks must pass to graduate from canary.
Carlos (CS): customers will ask for SLAs. can we offer a temporary SLA for canary cohort?
Nora Eng: we can offer a canary SLA on latency if they buy a dedicated migration window; otherwise no hard SLA but we can surface trace + rollback triggers.
Anika Patel: sample rollout policy config for prod ops (for discussion):
```json
{
  "retire_notice_days": 60,
  "canary_duration_days": 14,
  "canary_traffic_percent": 10,
  "canary_quality_threshold_pct": -2,
  "latency_p95_multiplier": 1.2,
  "rollback_window_days": 30,
  "migration_credit_usd": 5000
}
```
Liam Cho: can we make the quality threshold configurable per-customer? some customers care about embed drift vs. LLM F1 differently.
Maya Rivera: yes, make per-customer eval suite required for exceptions. default to our standard benchmarks if they don't provide one.
Carlos (CS): timeline ask from ACME: they need a comms plan + in-console migration checklist. sales will push for a customer-facing migration playbook PDF.
Anika Patel: I'll own the comms + checklist draft. Nora, can you scope the engineering effort to implement the routing-by-tag + rate-limit mode?
Nora Eng: rough estimate: 3 engineer-weeks to add maintenance routing + 2 engineer-weeks for admin console controls and audit logs. adds a new flag `soft_retire=true` and a routing policy.
Liam Cho: also need acceptance gates in deploy pipeline to prevent accidental retire of pinned versions. add a preflight check that flags pinned routes.
Maya Rivera: ops question — how do we measure customer migration success? propose: pass rate on their eval suite, <10% increase in error-rate, and <15% token-cost delta.
Anika Patel: good — we'll include metrics in the playbook: canary_metrics = ["eval_pass_rate", "latency_p95", "error_rate", "token_cost_delta"]. set alert thresholds and auto-rollback triggers.
dev-bot: deploy-bot scheduled weekly: "model-retire-checker" will run nightly and post exceptions to #product if pinned models scheduled within 30d. :robot_face:
Carlos (CS): anything else from legal or finance? finance needs cost of migration credits mapped to discounts on invoice.
Anika Patel: ok will loop in finance after we finalize numbers. next steps: 1) finalize playbook language + thresholds (this week), 2) Nora to draft engineering scope and timeline (EOW), 3) CS to prepare customer comm template and checklist (EOW).
Liam Cho: +1. ping me when playbook is ready, I'll add preflight checks.
Maya Rivera: I'll draft benchmark gating docs and sample eval commands for customers. brief snippet for eval runner:
```
# run customer eval
python eval_runner.py --model candidate --suite acme_suite.json --baseline acme_baseline.json
```
Anika Patel: thanks all. filing this as a playbook draft — will post a cleaned version and assign owners. :thumbsup:
Carlos (CS): thanks — ACME wants to review draft before we ship. I'll coordinate.
Nora Eng: noted. linking engineering RFC once available.
Anika Patel: end of thread.
